review.verdict: PP1 completeness-relations lens on proposal 3709170e (version 2026-10-11.r1): no P0 or P1 findings, three P2 findings to correct before Samuel decides, and five P3 findings. I recomputed every relation by hand and all of them hold. Intake: 0 < 200 < 1000; 750 < 3000 < 4500; hold 4500 + 1000 = 5500; attempt 750 + 4500 + 1000 + 750 = 7000. Writer: 750 < 12000 < 16000; lock 6000 = gate 6000; gate 6000 >= 5500, a margin of 500 (it was 1000 in the nonproduction profile); gate + reserve 7000 < 12000 < 16000; release 16000 + 1000 = 17000; attempt 750 + 16000 + 1000 + 1500 = 19250. Every ceiling is at or below the accepted nonproduction values. The JSON and Markdown values match each other. Every value is labelled proposed and unmeasured, nothing is presented as measured, and no default is copied from the starter plan. Each relation the source checks (currentness.sql:1316-1325 and 1349-1362@264e6af; intake.sql:465-505@121d0987) is satisfied, and the effective writer lock_timeout is forced to exactly 6000. The three P2 findings: (1) the 7000ms statement-clock objective at the writer gate cannot be met with the proposed writer values once more than 5000ms has passed before the gate. One full permitted lock wait, including the normal wait behind an intake's row hold, already exceeds that, so this is a regression from the nonproduction profile. (2) The doc 78 LV-2 consequence for the whole writer route, and its catalog-wide reach, is not registered. (3) The private-session revoke has no stated lock-wait relation to the intake hold, and no class or values. The P3 findings cover gaps in which conditions are carried forward and in completeness: the two carriers' copies of the intake and writer limits must be equal; the revoke-reach limit CS-33 and the install-window limit CS-36 are not carried; install and rollback timers (TC-27) and a recovery bound (TC-28) are missing; there is no per-field map of what happens when each timer expires; the too-large rule is only implicit; effective-level relations are overclaimed; and the deadlock_timeout default and its privilege restriction need a caveat. Nothing was executed, and this review does not approve any live profile.

findings.title: Statement-clock gate headroom objective is unattainable with the proposed writer values; regression from the nonproduction relation
findings.claim: The proposal keeps an objective of at least 7000ms remaining 'on both clocks' at writer gate entry, and justifies writer statement 12000 as leaving '5000 beyond gate+reserve at statement origin'. The statement clock starts with the DML. The guard is an AFTER STATEMENT trigger, so the statement's own row-lock waits, each allowed up to the route lock_timeout of 6000, happen before the gate check. The objective therefore needs pre-gate elapsed <= 12000 - 7000 = 5000ms, which is less than one permitted lock wait (6000) and less than the intake whole hold (5500). A material writer that waits behind an intake's FOR SHARE on a lot, document, test, legal-binding or session-binding row for the full hold reaches the gate with 6500 < 7000. The source's transaction-only check admits gate entry up to 9000ms elapsed, where only 3000ms of statement time remains against a 6000ms gate wait. In the nonproduction profile the allowance was 15000 - 8000 = 7000, equal to its lock of 7000 and at least its hold of 6000. The production narrowing (statement -3000 against gate + reserve -1000) breaks a property the accepted profile had, and the rationale does not say so. The outcome is fail-closed (57014 or 55P03), so this is a refusal-rate and decision-transparency defect, not an unsafe relation.

findings.title: Doc 78 LV-2 route-wide writer lock_timeout consequence, now a single point, is not registered
findings.claim: Doc 78 LV-2 required the route-wide writer lock_timeout bound to be registered as a decision-3 blast-radius consequence. Under the accepted source the bound is a single point: carrier lock == gate, effective <= field, effective >= gate, so the effective value is exactly 6000ms. That value applies to every lock acquisition of every statement on every material-writer and owner-admin route, not only to gate waits, and any other value refuses all material platform writes, including before first publication, as well as publish, activation and revoke. In addition, statement, transaction and idle must equal the pg_db_role_setting values for the exact login-role/database pair. So 12000/16000/750 become the settings for every session of the writer login role, including unrelated traffic sharing it. Intake (3000/4500) and writer (12000/16000) catalog values differ, so the two classes cannot share one login-role/database pair, and on today's single shared service_role route at least one class always refuses (doc 78 QOE-01). json:388 states 'must equal6000ms', but neither the route-wide nor the role-wide reach is presented for Samuel's decision.

findings.title: Private-session revoke has no stated lock-wait relation to the intake row hold, and no values, refusal mapping or owner
findings.claim: Intake holds the private session row FOR SHARE for its whole transaction (up to the 5500ms hold). The session revoke is a separate row UPDATE that waits on that row under its route's lock_timeout. Doc 78 QOE-06 required either binding a route whose effective lock wait is at least the intake whole hold, or registering that private-session revoke may refuse while an intake on that session is in flight. The proposal offers only 'writer-equivalent outer ceilings'. That phrase does not say whether the lock wait is included, gives no values or route class, and no owner. operationalClasses omits the class entirely. If the revoke ran on an intake-class route (lock 200ms) it would refuse under any concurrent intake. The proposal notes that the existing logout returns HTTP 200 even when the durable revoke fails, so the user-visible logout would still report success.

Name the unit, class and route, the 55P03/57014 mapping, and the responsible session owner (via the coordinator, currently UNKNOWN), all still subject to that owner's review.

findings.title: Cross-carrier equality of the intake and writer sections is not stated
findings.claim: The writer carrier and the intake carrier each contain both intake and writer sections, and each source path checks the gate >= intake transaction + cleanup relation only within its own carrier. If the two independently frozen carriers differed (for example, the intake carrier allowing a longer intake transaction with a matching larger gate in its own copy), both would pass the source checks while the actual intake hold exceeded the actual writer gate. That would silently violate R2-7. json:411 binds only profileId/profileVersion.
findings.fix: State that both carriers' intake and writer sections must equal proposedLimits exactly, or at minimum that the intake carrier's intake fields are <= the writer carrier's intake fields. Make this a PPM-10 freeze check, because the source does not compare the two carriers.

findings.title: Revocation refusal reach (CS-33) and the install-window refusal (CS-36) are not restated for production
findings.claim: Emergency authority revoke depends on a valid writer carrier, matching identities, integrity, an effective lock_timeout of exactly 6000, and the absence of foreign or earlier gate holders. Writer-class holders can hold the gate for up to 17000ms against revoke's 6000ms wait. The proposal's platformConsequences names only material-write refusal. The proposal also repeats 'No guard installation until every affected writer has required valid configuration'. Under CS-36 that cannot be satisfied, because the anchor table is created inside the install transaction, so all material platform writes refuse until the owner's COMMENT. A write-freeze window or a reviewed amendment is required, and neither is mentioned.

findings.title: Effective-level relations overstated; deadlock_timeout default and privilege caveat missing
findings.claim: json:388 says 'Shorter effective values still require all relations', but the source re-checks only idle < statement < transaction, intake lock < deadlock, and writer lock >= gate at the effective level. It does not check gate + reserve < effective writer statement, so an installed shorter writer statement (for example, below 7000) would pass the source while every gate wait gets cut off by 57014. That rule therefore depends on qualification, not on the source. Separately, deadlockTimeoutMs 1000 equals PostgreSQL's documented default (1s), and the parameter can be changed only by superusers or holders of SET privilege. The target's effective value may be provider-controlled, and a passing readback would not show that anyone configured or measured it.

verdicts.note: Recomputed: writer statement 12000 - (gate 6000 + reserve 1000) = 5000ms of pre-gate allowance. That is below writer lock 6000 and below the intake whole hold 4500 + 1000 = 5500. In the nonproduction profile it was 15000 - 8000 = 7000, equal to its lock of 7000 and at least its hold of 6000 (NP json:158-170@9c4a9b5). The guard is an AFTER ... FOR EACH STATEMENT trigger (currentness.sql:1378-1379@264e6af), and intake holds the lot, document and test rows (intake.sql:608,627-628@121d0987) and the session-binding and legal-binding rows (:572-573) FOR SHARE. So a writer that waits the full hold arrives at the gate with 6500 < 7000. Two corrections to the lens. (a) The 5000 figure is already disclosed (md:67, json:213@3709170e). What is missing is its comparison with lock and hold, and CS-30's fix of registering 57014-at-gate as an expected refusal class (80 json:2500-2509). (b) Source admitting gate entry with only 3000ms of statement time left is not a regression: the NP transaction check also admits entry at 12000 elapsed with 15000 - 12000 = 3000 left. Reasoned, not run: the carrier requires singleRpcAutocommit=true (currentness.sql:1298), so the statement and transaction clocks start almost together. The statement clock therefore always binds first, and the transaction-age check at :1360-1363 (entry up to 9000 elapsed) never does. The problem is structural, not an edge case. It fails closed, so P2 transparency, not P1.

Confirmed. The LV-2 fix explicitly asks that this route-wide lower and upper bound be registered as a decision-3 blast-radius consequence (78 json:1197-1199). The proposal only says the lock 'must equal6000ms' (json:388) and that 'shared pools may affect unrelated transactions' (json:826). Source forces distinct login-role/database pairs: each pair holds one approved_limits key (currentness.sql:1248-1252), intake requires routeClass 'intake' (intake.sql:416@121d0987) and writer requires 'writer' (currentness.sql:1268,1572,1779). Doc 78 S4's 'Distinct routes per class, or a reviewed amendment' (78 MD:233) is not restated. Supporting evidence from supabase.com/docs/guides/database/postgres/timeouts (fetched, NOT RUN): PostgREST connects as `authenticator`, and service_role falls back to authenticator's 8s statement_timeout. On the only known route (doc 78 QOE-01's shared service_role client), the writer startup statement, transaction and idle values would therefore apply to authenticator, which serves all API traffic, and only one of the two classes could use that pair. Minor citation slip: effective<=field is :1335-1336, not :1342-1343.

Downgraded from P2. Doc 78 QOE-06 gives the session owner the S4 job of binding a sufficient wait or registering the delay (78 MD:94). The proposal registers the delay: 'Private-session revoke is a distinct row UPDATE that can wait behind the earlier session share lock' (md:206). It also discloses that logout returns 200 (md:117) and carries QOE-06 as PPM-08 (json:907-914). The NP profile also gave no session-revoke values (NP json:397). What remains is precision: say that 'writer-equivalent outer ceilings' includes an effective lock wait of at least 5500 (writer 6000 meets that), or say that the revoke may refuse with 55P03 while an intake holds the row (intake.sql:631).

Verified. Intake checks gate >= intake transaction + cleanup only inside its own carrier (intake.sql:471@121d0987), and the writer does the same inside the writer carrier (currentness.sql:1323@264e6af). profileVersion binding (json:411) does not compare values. Divergent carriers would break R2-7 without either check noticing. The outcome is writer 55P03 refusals, which fail closed, so P3 is right.

Upheld, narrowed. Revoke failure is partly covered already: 'A timeout is not successful revocation' (md:206) and 'Failed/uncertain revoke stays administratively disabled' (json:835). Still missing: CS-33, that revoke depends on profile validity, integrity and identity (80 json:2533-2542); and CS-36, that the anchor cannot be supplied inside the install transaction (80 json:2566-2575). Because of CS-36, the rule 'No guard is to be installed before every affected writer has required valid configuration' (md:165, json:826) cannot be met without a write-freeze window or an amendment.

Verified TC-27 (install/rollback DDL with no timer admission, 83 json:2515-2524) and TC-28 (unbounded recovery read, 83 json:2526-2535). Neither is proposed or carried. md:31 leaves Docs83-86 in force, but a production timer profile is the natural place to propose install, rollback and recovery bounds, or to carry them as S4 items. Removing replay from the intake class (NP json:121 vs json:328) is consistent with C-7, which leaves TC-28's bound without an owner. The point that writer acquisition, response and attempt have no consumer on existing platform routes is valid.

Narrowed. The refusals section already maps SQLSTATEs: 55P03/40P01/40001 to retryable 503; 25P03/25P04 and after-transmission expiry to OUTCOME_UNCERTAIN; 57014 not safe-retry proof (json:831-833). The real gaps are: the per-field link in fieldDecisions; acquisition and response expiry before versus after transmission; the HTTP mapping of gate 55P03/57014 on existing writer routes; and the dropped 24000 global maximum (NP json:295-296). 'safe-integer' is stricter than source's int64 bound, so it is a carrier-authoring rule, not an inconsistency. It only needs a note that source does not enforce it.

Upheld, reframed. json:388 is a normative requirement, and md:106 correctly describes what the SQL checks, so the proposal does not overclaim source enforcement. What is missing is who enforces gate+reserve < effective writer statement. Source checks it on the carrier only (currentness.sql:1325) and not on effective values (:1349-1352). Concrete case: with Supabase's documented 8s authenticator default (supabase.com/docs, NOT RUN), an effective writer statement of 8000 passes source (<= 12000; 750 < 8000 < transaction) and leaves 1000ms of pre-gate allowance. The deadlock_timeout caveat (1s server default, superuser or SET privilege needed) is valid as the lens quoted it.

review.verdict:
PP2 (enforcement, routing and anchor), r1 at 3709170e / records 31de10e8: CORRECTIONS RECOMMENDED BEFORE SAMUEL'S DECISION. No P0 and no P1. Six P2 and five P3.

The proposal is honest:
- Every value is labelled UNMEASURED, and every installed value is UNKNOWN.
- No production default is presented as measured.
- Nothing authorizes installation, activation or reactivation. One P3 wording ambiguity is at MD:15.

Its gaps are in routing and operation, where unchanged source forces consequences the proposal leaves out.
- **Anchor tuple (PP2-1).** It offers a "legitimate common tuple" that the source makes impossible without giving the application owner privileges, and it omits CS-35's anchor-rotation option.
- **Emergency revoke (PP2-2).** It does not record that revoke depends on the anchor and profile (CS-33).
- **Class routes (PP2-3).** It does not carry doc 78 U-3. The source in fact requires a distinct login role per class.
- **Blast radius (PP2-4).** It does not disclose that the session-terminating timers apply to every session of each class's login route.
- **Install precondition (PP2-5).** CS-36 makes "valid configuration before guards" impossible as written.
- **Writer bound (PP2-6).** The headline 19,250 ms writer/admin bound has no enforcement point in source.

Bindings checked from Git:
- Blobs b9f44603 (54,645 bytes) and 3b5d2b24 (31,671 bytes) match the registration.
- Trees 839d8b68 and 9a32da27 match the registration.
- Records commit 31de10e8 does not touch either proposal path.
- Raw SHA-256 was not recomputed, because no hashing tool was permitted.

NOT RUN. Read-only.

findings.title: PPM-03 offers a common writer/admin tuple the source makes unreachable without owner privileges, and omits CS-35's rotation option
findings.claim:
Under unchanged source, one global anchor seals exactly one carrier. That carrier binds loginRole=session_user, requestRole=current_setting('role') or session_user, and ownerRole=current_user=O.

The owner functions publish, activation and revoke are SECURITY INVOKER and refuse unless current_user is O. The material guard is SECURITY DEFINER and sees the writer's role GUC (for example service_role). For one tuple to admit both, the application writers would need request role O, or would need to log in as O. Both give the application route owner privileges, which the proposal itself forbids.

So the 'legitimate unchanged-source common routing' offered in PPM-03 has no legitimate solution. The only unchanged-source option is CS-35's per-operation anchor rotation by the owner, and the proposal omits it. Rotation has consequences of its own: while the anchor seals the admin tuple, every material platform write refuses, including before publication. The JSON:970 approval condition 'bound to ... compatible routes' therefore cannot be met without rotation or an amendment.
findings.fix: Restate PPM-03 and §5. Under unchanged source, a common tuple requires application owner privileges and is therefore excluded. The only unchanged-source path is owner per-operation anchor rotation. Name its consequences: material writes refuse while the admin tuple is anchored; the owner performs and records each rotation; and every rotation needs its own frozen carrier digest. Otherwise require the separately reviewed amendment (a set of per-route carrier digests). Bind this choice into the live-profile decision text.

findings.title: Emergency and administrative revocation omit CS-33: revoke depends on integrity, a valid profile and the anchor sealing the owner's tuple
findings.claim:
The revocation and hold text says only that revoke takes no table locks, that a timeout is not revocation, and that app disable comes first.

Revoke first runs integrity(). It then requires a valid writer carrier at its own login, an anchor equal to that carrier's SHA-256, and an identity match that includes requestRole and ownerRole. It also requires at least gate+reserve (7,000 ms) of transaction budget remaining, and a gate acquired within lock_timeout.

In steady state the anchor must seal the material-writer tuple, or platform writes refuse. In that state the owner's revoke refuses with 55000 until the owner rewrites the anchor COMMENT, and rewriting it in turn refuses all material writes. The same refusal follows from any carrier or integrity drift.

The decision-3 consequence that missing or invalid writer limits refuse revoke as well as material writes is not stated. JSON:829 says only 'refuses new admission'. CS-33 is not named.

The pg_db_role_setting row for a (login, database) pair carries exactly one approved_limits value. Intake refuses unless routeClass='intake', and every writer/admin path refuses unless routeClass='writer'. So intake and writer need distinct session_user login roles, not just distinct pools.

The proposed values also make a single route refuse one class. Intake needs an effective transaction_timeout of at most 4,500 ms, equal to the catalog. A writer needs at least 7,000 ms remaining at the gate.

The Quick Order intent, all 24 mapped writer routes, the rate limiter and early-access session persistence all go through one shared service_role admin client. Production operation therefore requires a new class route through excluded seams, or a reviewed amendment.

The proposal says the decision does not approve a new connection design (MD:15), but never says that operation is impossible without one. It also does not carry QOE-01's 'no blanket shared-role timeout change'.

The current shared client cannot carry both classes, so operation needs a separately authorized class route through the excluded seams (server/supabase.ts, server/index.ts, production-deps.ts and the writer files) or a reviewed amendment. findings.title: Session-terminating timers bind every session of each class's login route, and the proposal does not disclose it
findings.claim:
The source requires effective statement, transaction and idle values to equal the login role's role-in-database catalog settings. That makes pre-BEGIN arming a login-route-wide setting, not a per-request one.

Every other session of that login in that database inherits the class values. In PG17, transaction_timeout and idle_in_transaction_session_timeout terminate the whole session, which kills the pooled physical connection and any unrelated work on it.

Supabase documents one designated login user per API server. If a class uses that login, all API traffic gets transaction 4,500 ms, idle 750 ms and statement 3,000 ms for intake, or 16,000 ms, 750 ms and 12,000 ms for writers. If the owner's ordinary login carries the admin carrier, migrations, installation and maintenance inherit 16,000 ms and 750 ms.

Whichever route hosts logout or session revoke inherits that class's lock_timeout. On the intake route that is 200 ms, against an intake hold of 5,500 ms, while logout still returns HTTP 200.

'Blast radius' in the proposal refers only to lock exposure.

upheld.title: Writer statement value makes the retained 7000ms statement-clock gate objective unattainable under normal contention; regression from the nonproduction relation
upheld.claim:
**The arithmetic.** Writer statement 12000 - (gate 6000 + reserve 1000) leaves 5000ms of pre-gate statement allowance. That is below one permitted writer row-lock wait (lock = gate = 6000) and below the intake whole hold (4500 + 1000 = 5500).

**Why the row waits count.** The guard is an AFTER ... FOR EACH STATEMENT trigger (currentness.sql:1378-1379). The DML's own row waits therefore come before the gate check. Intake holds rows FOR SHARE for up to 5500ms: lots, documents and tests (intake.sql:608, :627-628), and session-binding and legal-binding rows (:572-573). A writer that waits one full intake hold reaches the gate with at most 6500ms of statement time, which is less than 7000.

**Why it is structural.** The carrier attests singleRpcAutocommit, so the statement and transaction clocks start almost together. The statement clock therefore always binds before the source's transaction-only remainder check, which admits entry up to 9000ms elapsed (:1357-1363). The shortfall is structural, not an edge case.

**The regression.** The nonproduction profile satisfied statement >= lock + gate + reserve (15000 = 7000 + 7000 + 1000), and its 7000ms allowance was at least its 6000ms hold. Production fails both: 12000 < 13000, and 5000 < 5500.

**What the proposal says.** md:67 and json:213 state the 5000 figure only 'at statement origin'. md:104, json:355 and PPM-05 keep a 7000ms objective 'on both clocks' without deriving that the proposed values defeat it. CS-30's fix, to register 57014 at the gate as an expected refusal class, is not carried.

**Severity.** The outcome fails closed (57014 or 55P03), so this is P2 decision transparency, not an unsafe relation.

**Rejected sub-claim.** Gate entry with only 3000ms of statement time left is not new; the nonproduction profile had the same.
upheld.fix:
Choose no value. Add the derived bound: the maximum pre-gate statement time that still meets the objective = writer.statementTimeoutMs - gateWaitMs - postGateReserveMs = 5000. Say that this is below writer.lockTimeoutMs (6000) and the intake hold (5500).

Then present Samuel with exactly one of:
- **(a) A carrier-level relation.** writer.statementTimeoutMs >= writer.lockTimeoutMs + gateWaitMs + postGateReserveMs, which is the nonproduction property. A weaker form is >= intake hold + gateWaitMs + postGateReserveMs. Statement must stay below transaction, and the attempt sum must be recomputed.
- **(b) Withdrawal.** Withdraw minimumStatementRemainingAtWriterGateProposalMs as an objective. Register 57014 at the gate, including statement-clock refusal after a full permitted row wait, as an expected writer and admin refusal class under CS-30, with an S3 control.

critic.samuelDecisionPoints:
Samuel decides the following. This review chooses no value and authorizes nothing.

1. **Numeric profile.** Whether to adopt the intake and writer values (lock, statement, transaction, idle, deadlock, cleanup, acquisition, response, attempt, gate, reserve) once corrected. In particular:
   - the PP-1 choice: either a carrier relation writer.statement >= writer.lock + gate + reserve (the nonproduction property), or accepting 57014 at the gate as an expected writer and admin refusal class (CS-30);
   - the gate-over-hold margin of 500ms (nonproduction 1000);
   - how acquisitionMs is represented and enforced (PP-12).

2. **Platform consequences to accept.**
   - Material writes refuse when limits are missing or invalid, including before publication; revoke also refuses (already accepted under r3 decision 3).
   - Effective writer lock_timeout equals the gate on every writer and admin route.
   - Class timers, TimeZone and DateStyle become role-wide startup settings, and timer expiry terminates sessions.
   - Publish and activation SHARE locks stall platform DML for up to 17000ms, and NOWAIT refusals happen during maintenance.
   - Intake refusal exposure is up to 17000ms per writer-class transaction.
   - All material writes refuse in a write-freeze window between install and the owner's anchor COMMENT.

3. **Routing and anchor path.**
   - Distinct class login routes, which need a separately authorized connection design through excluded seams, or a reviewed amendment.
   - For writer and admin, one of: the application request role equals O (only if already true; no grants), owner per-operation anchor rotation with its refusal windows, or a reviewed per-route-digest amendment.

4. **Writer end-to-end bound.** Accept that only the database timers bound writers and owner administration (17000ms release target), or separately authorize writer-route deadline changes later.

5. **Private-session revoke.** Bind an effective wait of at least 5500ms, or accept refusal or delay while an intake holds the row, with logout still returning HTTP 200.

6. **Reactivation responsibility.** Samuel alone approves any live reactivation, with no automatic reactivation. Revoked revisions need a new revision. Under later explicit authority the sequence is: disable new admission first, then revoke, then verify. The live reactivation operator is UNKNOWN (json:965) and must be designated.

7. **Activation and installation operators.** Designate, through the coordinator, the actual database owner O, the configuration installer, the configuration artifact owner and the live activation/reactivation operator. All are UNKNOWN (json:962-966).

8. **Binding.** The live-profile decision must bind this exact version and its raw digest (or a corrected successor), plus the named evidence.
